title: Rabbi David Tawil: Yehoshua Chapter 5- "Circumcision & Pesah- Our National Identities"

chapters.title: Introduction and personal connection
chapters.about: Rabbi Tawil introduces Yehoshua chapter 5 and his personal family news.

chapters.title: Preparations for conquest
chapters.about: The Jewish people cross the Jordan and prepare for the rituals of Brit Mila and korban Pesach.

chapters.title: The ritual of mass circumcision
chapters.about: Yeshua performs mass circumcision at Gilgal, addressing why it was dormant in the wilderness.

chapters.title: Reasons for the wilderness delay
chapters.about: Discussion of Rashi and other commentaries regarding danger and the lack of circumcision.

chapters.title: Korban Pesach and the end of man
chapters.about: The nation performs the korban Pesach and begins eating the produce of the land.

chapters.title: The significance of the two rituals
chapters.about: Connecting Brit Mila and korban Pesach as foundational to national identity and the mission of Am Israel.

chapters.title: Yeshua and the angel
chapters.about: Analysis of the encounter between Yeshua and the angel of God at the edge of Jericho.

summary: Rabbi Tawil explores the significance of the Brit Mila and the korban Pesach performed by the Jewish people upon entering the land of Israel in Yehoshua chapter 5. He discusses how these rituals serve as markers of national identity and mission, and examines the cryptic encounter between Yeshua and an angel that emphasizes the holiness of the land before the upcoming conquest.
questions: Why did the Jewish people not perform circumcision during their 40 years in the wilderness?
Why are Brit Mila and korban Pesach considered essential markers of Jewish identity?
What is the connection between the removal of shoes in the presence of the angel and the holiness of the land?
Why does the Torah link the performance of these rituals to the consequence of karet?
How does the transition from man to the produce of the land reflect the shift from a miraculous to a natural existence?
